title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll picked Container Terminal. Keep it, take an alternative, or roll again.

options.label: Container Terminal
options.lineage: Deep-water container ports and ISO 6346 box markings: the world Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and Iceberg are literally named after
options.thesis: A data platform is a port: cargo comes in from every source, gets stacked, tracked and shipped on time. Isa runs the terminal.
options.viewport: A daylight quay. A gantry crane lowers corrugated containers onto a stack while the name ISA INALCIK is stencilled on the lead box in a code like ALTQ 2013 7. Below the stack, a manifest strip lists role, location and the LinkedIn and GitHub links.
options.risk: If the crane drops become decoration rather than navigation, the page turns into a themed costume. Every box has to stay a real, clickable project or role.

raised.raise: The career runs as one unbroken quay line from 2006 to now, with a running beacon light parked on the present.
Everything registers to one quay edge, an off-centre rail. Nothing floats free of it.
Hard-edged boxes on one strict grid, and a door that physically swings open on press.

options.label: Lineage DAG
options.lineage: dbt docs and Airflow lineage graphs
options.thesis: Career, projects and contributions as one lineage graph that runs green node by node as you scroll.
options.viewport: A dark canvas with the name as the root node and edges fanning out to Allianz, BestSecret, Trino and dbt-hodor, all lighting green.
options.risk: This is where most data-engineer portfolios land: dark, node graph, neon green.

options.label: Crouwel grid specimen
options.thesis: The name built cell by cell on a visible construction grid, so the page proves systematic engineering.
options.viewport: Monumental ISA INALCIK assembled from grid cells, with the work listed as a catalog below.
options.case: Holds on clarity (systematic, precise) but loses on audience identification, because data people don't see themselves in type specimens.
options.risk: Reads as a designer's portfolio, not an engineer's.

options.label: Neubrutalist grid
options.thesis: Hard black borders and offset shadows on a strict grid.
options.case: Clear, but generic: nothing about it says data platforms.
options.kept: Strict grid discipline and a physical press state.

options.label: Drum machine step row
options.thesis: Sixteen step keys under a chase light.
options.viewport: A step row as the timeline.
options.case: Fun, but the audience doesn't identify with it and the product isn't music.
options.kept: One unbroken line with a light that always marks now.

options.label: Emission-line rail
options.thesis: Hairline emission lines on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: A spectral band with ticks for destinations.
options.case: Too abstract for hiring managers and clients.
options.kept: Everything registers to one off-centre rail.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio: photo, headline, project cards, timeline, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Portrait and headline left, links right, project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other engineer's page.
